hypotheses.name: Stepover/relay-zone distance-transform saddle emission
layers: existing_faults.tif catalogue geometry only (distance-transform saddle field)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Blind normal faults nucleate at stepovers/relay ramps between mapped catalogue fault segments. These appear as saddle points in the Euclidean distance-to-catalogue transform: high distance to any mapped trace (concealed, >1 km off catalogue) but with fault segments approaching from multiple azimuths (a stepover between two parallel segments). Weight = dist^k * (number of quadrants containing catalogue faults within a 150 m window).
hypotheses.why_catches_uncatalogued: Targets concealed cross-faults and relay structures in the interiors of fault-bounded basins that no surface geologic map or USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue trace records. H33 and the D28/H27-4 lineage place dots across the catalogue collar + far field but do not specifically concentrate on multi-azimuth stepover saddles; H86Q basin-center ridges target single-direction equidistance (basin center), not the multi-segment stepover geometry.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Differs from H86Q (basin-center distance RIDGES, single equidistance direction, d_cat > 10 px) by targeting multi-azimuth stepover SADDLES between catalogue segments. Differs from all collar-prune (PRUNE), density (CONCENTRATION), relief (RELIEF), spacing (SPACING), and trace-bridge (TRACKB) lanes which use 19-band features or catalogue-proximal rules. Uses only catalogue geometry like H86Q but a different structural position.
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Qualitative only — no holdout possible (training_features.tif/labels.tif absent). No numeric projection claimed.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low — catalogue geometry only, ~100 lines, no 19-band stack, no GPU.
hypotheses.data_needed: existing_faults.tif + sample_submission.tif (both present in data/bridge/). No external data required.

hypotheses.name: Far-field catalogue-collar exclusion with adaptive Poisson-disc at kernel-gap scale
hypotheses.physical_signature: Under the 300 m DTI kernel (alpha=0.2, beta=0.8), FP_w sums every positive pixel while TP_w takes a max over each 3-px disk. Dots within 1-3 px of the catalogue (collar) contribute FP without new TP. H33 removed 2,545 collar dots at 1<d_cat<=2 px. This lane extends exclusion to d_cat <= 3 px and re-places the mass at the largest kernel gaps (>300 m from any other dot) in the far field, using adaptive Poisson-disc spacing equal to the kernel diameter.
hypotheses.why_catches_uncatalogued: Places all mass >3 px off catalogue (>300 m), concentrating on unmapped ground far from catalogue traces where concealed faults live. The H33 lineage still retains ~30% of dots within 1 km; this lane pushes to ~70-75% far-field while preserving kernel coverage.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Extends PRUNE's collar prune (1-2 px) to a hard 3 px exclusion with kernel-gap re-placement; differs from CONCENTRATION density redistribution (which keeps mass on H19-5 support) and from H86Q ridge emission (ridge-positioned, not gap-positioned).

hypotheses.name: Multi-scale curvature proxy from DEM-derived smoothed elevation (band 12 det_elev + band 19 det_elev_slope) if feature stack restored
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fault scarps produce local curvature sign changes (convex ridge / concave swale) at the 100 m DEM scale. A curvature proxy = Laplacian of smoothed det_elev combined with det_elev_slope sign, masked to off-catalogue pixels. Targets blind scarps with no mapped trace.
hypotheses.why_catches_uncatalogued: Catches subtle scarps of blind faults that lack surface expression sufficient for catalogue mapping but leave a 100 m DEM curvature signature.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Requires the 19-band training stack (absent in this checkout). Not yet implemented in any lane. Differs from relief (RELIEF) which uses tercile regime masking, not curvature sign.
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Qualitative only — blocked by absent feature stack.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium — requires shared template feature cache / training_features.tif restore (currently absent).
hypotheses.data_needed: training_features.tif (bands 12, 19) — NOT present; requires scripts/download_competition_data.sh on an unrestricted machine + prepare_data.py. Blocker.

hypotheses.name: Total-count wash-blanket depletion asymmetry across piedmont breaks (Band 6 tc downslope one-sided)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Hydrothermal alteration and fault-related clay reduce potassium/total count radiometrics. A one-sided downslope total-count depletion gradient across subtle piedmont breaks marks concealed fault-controlled alteration halos with no surface trace.
hypotheses.why_catches_uncatalogued: Targets concealed alteration-bounded faults buried under piedmont alluvium — invisible to surface mapping but radiometrically expressive.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Differs from TCWB (which used total count wash) by adding a one-sided downslope asymmetry and piedmont-break mask. Requires 19-band stack (absent).
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Qualitative only — blocked by absent feature stack.

hypotheses.name: Vector-gravity signed basement-depth footwall hinge kink (Band 15 depth_to_base_surf x Bands 11/18 gravity)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Listric normal faults roll over at depth, creating a footwall hinge kink in basement depth. The vector-gravity-signed cross-strike derivative of depth_to_base_surf, pulled up-dip by adaptive cot(dip), targets concealed listric fault tips missing from the catalogue.
hypotheses.why_catches_uncatalogued: Targets blind listric fault tips at depth with no surface rupture — structurally distinct from mapped range-front traces.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Differs from TCWB basement kink by using vector gravity (vg + hg) admittance and cot(dip) pullback. Requires 19-band stack (absent).
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Qualitative only — blocked by absent feature stack.
